subject.title: feat: provider fallback by failure class — quarantine auth-broken providers

question: Should generic 401/token-refresh failures become default auth-broken provider/profile quarantine, and what redacted status surface should expose that state?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing default fail-closed quarantine versus transient recovery affects compatibility, operator visibility, and security redaction semantics.

options.title: Define conservative hard-auth quarantine
options.body: Choose explicit signals for hard auth, require a confirming retry or refresh failure before quarantine, and expose a redacted provider-health status block.

options.title: Keep compatibility default and improve visibility
options.body: Keep current retry/cooldown behavior as the default while adding clearer `status`/Doctor diagnostics and optional stricter policy later.

options.title: Split into narrower incidents
options.body: Track the single-provider restart/config-write behavior and Codex OAuth wedge separately while leaving this issue as the broader policy discussion.

recommendation.title: Define conservative hard-auth quarantine
recommendation.body: Choose explicit signals for hard auth, require a confirming retry or refresh failure before quarantine, and expose a redacted provider-health status block.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main ownership and PR 100191 place this account closest to the fallback/auth/status decision surface.
